13.body:
load("@rules_julia//julia:defs.bzl", "julia_artifact") julia_artifact(name, srcs, out, artifact_name, files, lazy, platform_tags, strip_prefix, url) Build a Julia artifact from Bazel targets. Julia distributes binaries and data as artifacts: gzipped tarballs identified by the git tree hash of their contents and listed in a package's Artifacts.toml with a download URL and SHA-256. This rule produces both halves: the tarball, packed with the same Tar and 7z Julia itself uses, and an Artifacts.toml holding the entry for it, with both hashes computed by the code Pkg uses to verify downloads. Upload the tarball to the URL and merge the entry into the package's Artifacts.toml; Pkg and artifact"name" then install it like any other artifact. Files from srcs keep their path relative to the package (or strip_prefix below it); files places outputs from anywhere at an explicit path. Directories (tree artifacts) are copied whole. Platform specific artifacts set platform_tags. The values are taken from the target platform (os, arch) and the @rules_julia//julia/settings flags (libc, libgfortran_version, cxxstring_abi), so building the same target under several --platforms yields one entry per platform, ready to be concatenated. Platform independent artifacts (data, models, ...) leave it empty. Example: julia_artifact( name = "libfoo", srcs = ["include/foo.h"], files = {":libfoo_shared": "lib/libfoo.so"}, platform_tags = ["os", "arch", "libc"], url = "https://github.com/me/Foo.jl/releases/download/v1.0.0/{file}",
) produces libfoo.tar.gz and libfoo.Artifacts.toml: [[libfoo]]
arch = "x86_64"
git-tree-sha1 = "..."
libc = "glibc"
os = "linux" [[libfoo.download]] sha256 = "..." url = "https://github.com/me/Foo.jl/releases/download/v1.0.0/libfoo.tar.gz" ATTRIBUTES Name Description Type Mandatory Default name A unique name for this target. Name required srcs Files to include at their path relative to the package, or to strip_prefix within it. List of labels optional [] out The tarball to write. Defaults to <name>.tar.gz. Label; nonconfigurable optional None artifact_name The artifact's name in Artifacts.toml. Defaults to the target name. String optional "" files Files or directories to place at an explicit path inside the artifact, mapping each label to its destination. . places a directory's contents at the root. Dictionary: Label -> String optional {} lazy Mark the artifact lazy, so Julia only downloads it on first use. Boolean optional False platform_tags Platform tags to record, any of os, arch, libc, libgfortran_version and cxxstring_abi. Empty for platform independent artifacts. libc is only recorded on Linux. List of strings optional [] strip_prefix A directory below the package that srcs paths are made relative to. String optional "" url The URL the tarball will be downloadable from, recorded in the entry. {file} expands to the tarball's file name. Without it the entry has no download table. String optional ""

3.body:
Targets follow Julia's conventions. A julia_library named Foo is loaded with using Foo from src/Foo.jl (or Foo.jl next to the BUILD.bazel file). When the package directory also holds a Project.toml, list it in data so Julia loads the package through it. The package then has the name and UUID recorded there, which packages such as Preferences and package extensions depend on, and its dependencies resolve from the [deps] table: julia_library( name = "Foo", srcs = glob(["src/**/*.jl"]), data = ["Project.toml"], deps = ["@deps//:JSON"],
) Packages installed by the pkg extension are always set up this way.

30.body: --@rules_julia//julia/settings:linker The linker used to turn a system image object archive into a shared library. toolchain (default): whatever the resolved Julia toolchain's linker attribute says (julia for toolchains registered by the julia extension unless a julia.toolchain(linker = ...) tag says otherwise). julia: the lld bundled with Julia, invoked through Base.Linking exactly as Julia links its own package images. Works on every platform Julia ships for and needs no C++ toolchain. cc: cc_common.link with the resolved C++ toolchain. Requires a GNU-compatible toolchain; fails if no C++ toolchain resolves. PARAMETERS Name Description Options name - "linker"

31.body: --@rules_julia//julia/settings:version The version of julia to use. Besides the flag, a config_setting named version_<major>.<minor>.<patch> is defined per known release and a version_<major>.<minor> setting per minor version matching any of its releases. Package graphs resolved for a Julia minor version are selected with the latter. PARAMETERS Name Description Options name The name of the flag. "version"

36.body:
load("@rules_julia//julia/pkg:defs.bzl", "julia_pkg_resolve") julia_pkg_resolve(name, manifest_bazel_json, manifests, project_toml) A rule for resolving Julia manifests from Project.toml using Julia's Pkg manager. Running the target resolves the project once per manifest listed in manifests, each time with a Julia toolchain of the version the manifest is declared for, and writes the results in place. Pkg resolves against one Julia version (its standard libraries, compat bounds and manifest format), so a project supporting several Julia minor versions carries one manifest per version, following Pkg's own Manifest-v<major>.<minor>.toml convention. Pass the manifests to the pkg module extension via pkg.from_manifest(manifests = ...); no additional lockfile is required. Optionally, manifest_bazel_json may be set (with a single manifest) to also write a Manifest.bazel.json containing package URLs, integrity values and artifacts. Pass that file to pkg.from_manifest(lockfile = ...) for modules consumed by other Bazel modules, since module extension facts are only persisted in the root module's MODULE.bazel.lock. Note that when setting this target up for the first time, empty manifest files need to be created. If you specify manifest_bazel_json, that file should also be created as an empty JSON object {}. Example: julia_pkg_resolve( name = "pkg_update", project_toml = "Project.toml", manifests = { "Manifest-v1.10.toml": "1.10", "Manifest-v1.12.toml": "1.12", },
) Then run: bazel run //:pkg_update Packages can be added to Project.toml at the same time: bazel run //:pkg_update -- --add JSON ATTRIBUTES Name Description Type Mandatory Default name A unique name for this target. Name required manifest_bazel_json An optional Manifest.bazel.json lockfile to generate/update with package URLs, integrity values and artifacts. Only supported with a single manifest. Label optional None manifests Julia manifests keyed by the Julia version each is resolved with, e.g. {"Manifest-v1.10.toml": "1.10", "Manifest-v1.12.toml": "1.12"}. A project supporting a single Julia version lists one Manifest.toml. Each manifest is resolved and verified under a registered toolchain of that version (the newest known patch release when only a minor version is given), regardless of --@rules_julia//julia/settings:version. Dictionary: Label -> String required project_toml The Project.toml file describing dependencies. Label required

41.body: Fetch the Julia packages recorded in one or more Manifest.toml files, or in a Manifest.bazel.json. Exactly one of manifests (or the single-file alias manifest) or lockfile must be set. With manifests, the stock Manifest.toml files written by Pkg are the only lockfiles. Each manifest records the Julia version that resolved it; its packages are built for that Julia minor version and marked incompatible with others, and the hub selects among manifests with @rules_julia//julia/settings:version. A project supporting several Julia versions lists one manifest per minor version (Pkg's Manifest-v<major>.<minor>.toml convention); julia_pkg_resolve resolves them all. Package tarballs are fetched from pkg_server using the UUID and git tree hash recorded for each package. On Bazel 9 and newer the integrity value of every tarball and the artifacts each package declares are persisted in the facts section of MODULE.bazel.lock, so after the first evaluation no network access is needed to evaluate the extension. On older Bazel versions the generated repositories are recorded in MODULE.bazel.lock instead. With lockfile, a Manifest.bazel.json produced by julia_pkg_resolve provides URLs, integrity values and artifacts up front and the extension never touches the network. The lockfile carries no Julia version, so its packages are available under every version. Prefer this for modules consumed by others, since facts are only persisted in the root module's lockfile. Pkg itself never runs: the manifest is parsed in Starlark and every package is fetched by its recorded hash. Attributes Name Description Type Mandatory Default name The name of the hub repository to create. Name required lockfile A Manifest.bazel.json lockfile produced by julia_pkg_resolve. Mutually exclusive with manifests. Label optional None manifest A single Manifest.toml; shorthand for manifests = [...]. Label optional None manifests Manifest.toml files, one per supported Julia minor version. Mutually exclusive with lockfile. List of labels optional [] pkg_server The Julia package server to fetch tarballs from when manifests is set. String optional "https://pkg.julialang.org"

5.title: Several Julia versions

6.body: Many packages depend on prebuilt binaries or data shipped as Julia artifacts , most visibly the _jll packages wrapping C libraries. These are built by BinaryBuilder inside a cross compilation environment that cannot be reproduced in a Bazel action, so the published tarballs are consumed as-is, pinned by the SHA-256 and git tree hash recorded in each package's Artifacts.toml. The pkg extension defines a repository per artifact variant and selects one for the target platform at analysis time, so only the variant in use is ever downloaded. Operating system and CPU come from the target platform. The remaining ABI tags Julia uses to pick a variant are flags that default to what official Julia binaries are built with: Flag Values Default @rules_julia//julia/settings:libc glibc, musl glibc @rules_julia//julia/settings:libgfortran_version 3, 4, 5 5 @rules_julia//julia/settings:cxxstring_abi cxx03, cxx11 cxx11 Variants that differ only in tags the rules do not model (for example libstdcxx_version) resolve to the newest one, matching what Pkg picks on a current Julia. A package whose artifact has no variant for the target platform fails to analyze with a message listing the platforms it is available for. Lazy artifacts, which Julia itself only downloads on first use, are the exception: they are fetched like any other where a variant exists, and simply omitted on platforms without one, so a package that never touches the artifact there still builds. Code that does touch it fails at the point of use, as it would under Julia without network access. Artifact metadata is recorded next to the package integrity values, in MODULE.bazel.lock facts or in Manifest.bazel.json, so reading Artifacts.toml happens once per package version.
6.title: Artifacts

7.body:
Facts are only persisted in the root module's lockfile. A module consumed by other Bazel modules should instead ship a Manifest.bazel.json so consumers never download tarballs just to learn their hashes. Set manifest_bazel_json on julia_pkg_resolve to generate it and pass it to pkg.from_manifest as lockfile instead of manifest. pkg.from_manifest( name = "deps", lockfile = "//:Manifest.bazel.json",
)
7.title: Publishing a module

8.body:
Julia distributes binaries and large data as artifacts : gzipped tarballs identified by the git tree hash of their contents, listed in a package's Artifacts.toml with a download URL and SHA-256. There is no registry for them; any URL works, and GitHub releases are the usual host. julia_artifact builds one from Bazel targets, so a cc_binary, a generated data set or any other output becomes an artifact in exactly the form Pkg expects. The tarball is packed with the Tar and 7z Julia ships and both hashes come from the code Pkg uses to verify downloads: load("@rules_julia//julia:defs.bzl", "julia_artifact") julia_artifact( name = "libfoo", srcs = ["include/foo.h"], files = {":libfoo_shared": "lib/libfoo.so"}, platform_tags = ["os", "arch", "libc"], url = "https://github.com/me/Foo.jl/releases/download/v1.0.0/{file}",
) This produces libfoo.tar.gz and libfoo.Artifacts.toml: [[libfoo]]
arch = "x86_64"
git-tree-sha1 = "..."
libc = "glibc"
os = "linux" [[libfoo.download]] sha256 = "..." url = "https://github.com/me/Foo.jl/releases/download/v1.0.0/libfoo.tar.gz" Upload the tarball to the URL and merge the entry into the package's Artifacts.toml. Platform tags are read from the target platform and the @rules_julia//julia/settings flags, so building the same target under several --platforms gives one entry per platform to concatenate. Leave platform_tags empty for platform independent artifacts. Without url the entry has no download table, for filling in once the file is hosted. Packages themselves need no publishing step: Pkg installs a package from its git tree, so a repository built with these rules is registered with Registrator or LocalRegistry exactly like any other Julia package.
8.title: Publishing artifacts
